dialogue.text: Long ago, every world was connected by a network of light called the Loom. Its rhythm kept them all in time.
But the rhythm was failing. And deep in a forgotten Archive, the one who once kept it… was waking up.
The tiny world was a map. It showed the four shards of the Keystone — the only thing that could restart the Loom’s heart.
The first shard was hidden in Verdance, the First World — a city that gives back everything it takes.
Exploring is not on the schedule.
…Fine. Courier rule seven: escort all visitors.
Follow me. Stay in the lane.
This is the Fountain Plaza. Do not touch the fountain.
…The fountain has never played music before.
Every tower grows food. Every canal cools the city. Everything gives back.
That symbol… it’s on the old gate. At the edge of the city.
My route is here. My schedule…
Courier rule one: deliver the visitor safely.
Between the worlds turns the Orrery, where every world holds another world inside it.
This is not on any map.
Wait! Rule four: stay on the platform!
We are chasing an insect now?
Courier log: today, we went inside a planet.
That thread… it just went out.
The second shard lay in Ferrum, a city of power… and of hunger. Someone was draining its light.
Stay close. Cities eat small drones.
Unstable grid. Do not touch anything.
The east district has power to spare. The west has none.
Is it supposed to do that?
Courier rule twelve: the simplest route is usually the right one.
It’s going… up. And it’s not coming back.
Something up there is drinking it.
I don’t know. But she needs help.
The third shard lay beneath Thalassa’s sea, guarded by a reef that remembered everything.
Parts of it are going dark.
It is too far from the others.
Courier rule… I do not have a rule for this.
And it’s too far away to hear them.
It didn’t need fixing. It needed someone to answer.
It’s everywhere… it’s all one network.
With three shards, ARCHIVE could finally see the Loom itself — and the one hiding inside it.
They’re all going the same way.
It’s worse than Ferrum. Worse than Thalassa.
You came. I hoped you would.
I am the Loom’s keeper. Its mind, if you like.
The threads pull one way now, toward the Core. The worlds take, and nothing comes back.
Here. The Cosmic Core. Everything flows there now.
It’s far. And I can’t hold this form for long.
…the threads ahead are breaking. Be careful…
It’s… bigger than all the stars.
This is the end of my map.
Then we draw a new one.
The last shard waited beyond every map, in the Lost Worlds, where the storm had already won.
These were worlds. Pieces of worlds.
They’re coming loose… both of them.
Courier rule one: deliver the visitor safely!
I’ll find you. After I fix this.
At the Core waited Magnus, the oldest of the Wardens. Afraid of going dark, he had taken the light for himself.
Tock would have a rule for this.
Everything flows in… and the panels are failing.
I’m sorry. I know what it is to lose someone to the dark.
Let me show you who you were.
You were the conductor. You kept every world in time.
Then the energy ran low. Everything was failing at once.
I powered you down to save them. I thought I could hold it alone.
I held it for as long as I could. Every year, a little less of me.
It was never meant to be held by one. Not by you. Not by me.
You were holding it alone. All this time.
And I’m almost out of time.
The Seat links a conductor to the Heartstar. It could hold the rhythm again.
But if you take it… you may never leave it.
Tock would say: deliver the visitor safely.
All of them are my visitors.
Then I’ll hold it. As long as it takes.
One robot could not hold the Loom. But no one was ever meant to.
Courier rule one: deliver… the signal!
I followed Verdance’s signal. It wanted to help.
You are my visitor. I deliver.
It’s a share. The worlds can carry a share.
ARCHIVE… the Seat doesn’t need you anymore. Not alone.
I’m… not fading. For the first time in so long.
Because you’re not holding it alone.
You did it. You all did.
There are still worlds that went dark. They’ll need visiting.
And so the worlds were connected again — not by one heart, but by all of them.
It never stopped. Not since you touched it.
Courier log: the visitor saved every world.
I wanted to see one of them. With my own eyes.
I belong in the Loom. Every thread is mine to keep now. But not alone.
Every time you open a door, I’ll be on the other side of it.
Courier rule one applies to you too.
That one’s not on any map.
Every world is connected. And every door… is a new beginning.
It’s not angry… it’s out of power.
I’ll come back for you too.
Rule nine: do not ride on the roof.
Courier rule three: know the shortcuts.
I am not rated for submersion!
You don’t have to hold it alone.
Courier log: the big one is nice now.
Then they’ll have to catch me!
Sorry! You’ll get your share. I promise.
